method_outcomes.B12: Identified a paired degree/noise alignment invariant. If A >= kappa N and the symmetrically tilted form C_s(A,N) is nonnegative for one fixed s>0, then ||e^{-tA} Pi_{>=K}|| <= exp[-s K (1-exp(-kappa t/s))]. The proof uses monotonicity of ||e^{-sN}e^{-tA}f||^2 plus Jensen and a scalar comparison ODE.
method_outcomes.B20: Ordinary coercivity alone is insufficient: the explicit 2x2 family N_K=diag(0,K), A_K=[[1,-sqrt(K)],[-sqrt(K),2K]] satisfies A_K>=N_K but has only polynomial high-degree damping through a slow eigenmode, while its tilted form loses positivity for large K. Conversely, the prior weak-Ising Kato/Toda certificate supplies both ordinary coercivity and tilted positivity, so it now yields full high-source-degree damping on the same verified small-coupling class.
method_outcomes.B27: Sharpened the implication quantifiers. Under uniform aligned full-tail damping, bounded source LDA through D_n and Pi_2=o(D_n) imply bounded noisy LDA through the same D_n, with no degree loss. Vanishing source LDA plus the same pressure/alignment hypotheses imply total-variation convergence after every fixed positive noise time. This is sufficient and remains PARTIAL source-wide.

new_theorems: Tilted alignment full-tail theorem: A >= kappa N and C_s(A,N)>=0 imply ||S_t Pi_{>=K}|| <= exp[-sK(1-exp(-kappa t/s))].
2x2 obstruction: A>=N alone does not imply exponential high-source-degree damping.
